items.stem: Torque at the crankshaft is 200 N·m and the overall gear ratio to the wheels is 10:1 (ignoring losses). What is the approximate torque delivered at the wheels?

options.rationale: This divides by the ratio; a reduction ratio multiplies torque, it does not reduce it.
The ratio changes the torque; it is not unchanged through the gearing.
A 10:1 reduction multiplies crankshaft torque by 10, giving roughly 2000 N·m at the wheels.
Gear ratios multiply rather than add to the input torque.

items.explanation: A 10:1 reduction multiplies crankshaft torque by 10, giving roughly 2000 N·m at the wheels.

items.stem: A car travels at a steady speed on a level road. Which statement best describes the net longitudinal force on it?

options.text: The net force is large and forward, proportional to engine power
options.rationale: Steady speed means zero acceleration, so the net force is not large.

options.text: The net force is zero because tractive force balances resistance
options.rationale: At constant velocity acceleration is zero, so drive force equals the sum of rolling and aerodynamic resistance.

options.text: The net force is backward because drag always dominates
options.rationale: If drag dominated, the car would decelerate; at steady speed forces balance.

options.text: There is no force acting on the car at all
options.rationale: Several forces act; they simply sum to zero at constant speed.

items.explanation: At constant velocity acceleration is zero, so drive force equals the sum of rolling and aerodynamic resistance.

items.stem: A team wants to reduce a vehicle's steady-state fuel consumption at highway speed. Select TWO changes that directly reduce the dominant resistive losses at that speed.

options.rationale: Aerodynamic drag scales with speed squared and dominates at highway speed, so reducing Cd cuts the largest loss.

options.text: Reduce rolling resistance with low-resistance tyres
options.rationale: Rolling resistance is a significant steady-speed loss, so lower-resistance tyres directly reduce consumption.
Brake size affects stopping, not steady-state cruising losses.
Exhaust sound does not change the resistive forces the engine must overcome.
Cabin electronics have negligible effect on highway tractive losses.

items.explanation: Aerodynamic drag scales with speed squared and dominates at highway speed, so reducing Cd cuts the largest loss.
